Definition: The availability and presence of major cloud service providers (hyperscale and regional) operating in or serving the country with local or near-local infrastructure. Cloud availability determines access to scalable computing resources for government, business, and startups.
Value Name: Regional cloud availability zone nearby (same sub-region)
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: No source had been cited originally. Verified (2026) that AWS (af-south-1, Cape Town), Microsoft Azure (South Africa North/West) and Google Cloud (africa-south1, Johannesburg) all operate availability zones in South Africa — the nearest sub-region to Angola — which supports Code 3 (regional zone nearby). Angola itself only hosts a local cloud-connectivity node (Angola Cables' Clouds2Africa/AngoNAP Luanda, Tier III, per Angola Cables corporate materials) that peers with these hyperscalers rather than a hyperscaler edge location itself, so Code 4 (local presence) is not yet warranted. Original Value Code confirmed unchanged.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted legal or regulatory requirements mandating that certain categories of data (personal data, government data, financial data, or critical infrastructure data) be stored within national borders. Central to data sovereignty debates in Africa.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: Original claim of 'no requirements' is not supported: Banco Nacional de Angola's Aviso n.8/20 (2 April 2020) requires financial institutions to notify and obtain BNA approval before contracting cloud/data-processing services, disclose the hosting country, and meet data-security/access conditions — a binding sectoral (financial-sector) data-location control. Xalam Analytics' Angola Data Center Market Brief (July 2025) corroborates that Angola has 'no explicit, broad data localisation requirement' but that sectoral guidelines exist in banking and that banking/oil-and-gas data is mostly hosted locally in practice. Angola's Data Protection Law (Lei 22/11, 2011) additionally restricts cross-border personal-data transfers absent an adequacy finding or Data Protection Agency authorisation. Together this evidence matches Code 3 (sectoral requirements only, e.g. financial data), not Code 1 (no requirements) — Value Code revised upward from 1 to 3.
